methodology: Editorial recalibration of pressure indexes after a July 2026 primary-source sweep. Scores measure documented pressure, implementation and exposure, not event probability, intent or proof of a coordinated plan. Counter-signals and safeguards are retained in every assessment.

assessments.rationale: Online-safety, age-assurance and platform-governance rules now materially shape publication, discovery and access. The European Media Freedom Act and appeal duties are meaningful counter-safeguards.
assessments.counterSignal: Due-process, media-protection and platform-notification rules are expanding alongside restrictions.

assessments.rationale: Every EU Member State must provide an interoperable wallet, large-scale pilots cover public and private services, high-assurance onboarding standards are in force and age verification can integrate with the wallet.
assessments.counterSignal: Official design retains voluntary individual use, selective disclosure, open standards and privacy safeguards.

assessments.rationale: Security, health, cyber and resilience frameworks continue to normalise exceptional coordination and data sharing. Current rule-of-law standards explicitly warn that emergency measures must remain necessary, temporary and reviewable.
assessments.counterSignal: Council of Europe standards, courts, legislatures and sunset requirements remain active constraints.

assessments.rationale: June inflation, energy-price growth, weak real-income gains and tighter household credit standards show sustained pressure on ordinary households.
assessments.counterSignal: Inflation is below earlier crisis peaks and some real-income measures remain positive rather than collapsing.

assessments.rationale: EU house prices continued rising while banks tightened housing-loan standards and rejection pressure increased, worsening access for new buyers and leveraged households.
assessments.counterSignal: The evidence does not show uniform collapse, and conditions vary substantially by country and region.

assessments.rationale: Cash acceptance has declined while digital-euro rulebook and pilot work advances. Payment access is increasingly mediated through regulated digital infrastructure.
assessments.counterSignal: The ECB supports legal protection for cash and states the digital euro will complement cash, not use programmable-money restrictions.

assessments.rationale: Current ombudsman and rule-of-law monitoring continues to identify transparency, access-to-records and institutional trust problems across public bodies.
assessments.counterSignal: Independent oversight, annual reporting and expanding public document systems provide active disclosure routes.

assessments.rationale: The 2026 Rule of Law Report records continuing justice, corruption, media and checks-and-balances concerns across multiple jurisdictions.
assessments.counterSignal: Stronger EU anti-corruption rules and country reforms are active counter-pressure rather than evidence of universal institutional failure.

assessments.rationale: Identity wallets, strategic raw-material platforms, digital payments, platform governance, health credentials and critical infrastructure increasingly rely on coordinated public-private systems.
assessments.counterSignal: Public procurement rules, competition law, privacy regulation and open-source reference implementations can limit private authority.

assessments.rationale: Cyber criticality, regional grid weaknesses, climate hazards and dependence on connected systems remain material.
assessments.counterSignal: ENTSO-E found no systemic European electricity adequacy risk for summer 2026 and ENISA reports improving maturity.

assessments.rationale: EMA continues active shortage communications for important medicines, showing real supply and access pressure requiring coordinated mitigation.
assessments.counterSignal: The shortages network, substitutions and regulatory coordination are functioning and do not indicate universal healthcare collapse.

assessments.rationale: Energy prices were a leading contributor to June 2026 inflation and geopolitical shipping risks continue to affect fuel and production costs.
assessments.counterSignal: Renewable generation, storage, interconnection and official affordability measures can reduce exposure over time.

assessments.rationale: European drought, flood, heat and adaptation evidence has pushed water resilience into an active implementation priority across jurisdictions.
assessments.counterSignal: A formal Water Resilience Strategy, investment and adaptation programmes are now being implemented.

assessments.rationale: Shipping disruption, energy and logistics prices, sanctions and strategic raw-material dependencies continue to expose essential supply chains.
assessments.counterSignal: Global trade is still expanding and diversification, demand aggregation and storage mechanisms are being deployed.

assessments.rationale: Election networks now actively address information manipulation, political safety and AI use in elections, reflecting a material cross-border risk environment.
assessments.counterSignal: Independent election administration, judicial review, monitoring and anti-SLAPP protections remain operational safeguards.

assessments.rationale: ILO and OECD evidence shows widespread task transformation, changing skill demand and inequality risk as AI adoption accelerates.
assessments.counterSignal: Current empirical reviews find limited evidence of large-scale displacement so far; augmentation and productivity gains remain important.

assessments.rationale: The 2026 Rule of Law review continues to identify concentration, editorial-independence, state-advertising and journalist-safety concerns.
assessments.counterSignal: The European Media Freedom Act adds ownership, independence and platform-removal safeguards.

assessments.rationale: Australia is enforcing an under-16 restriction, UK age assurance operates at scale, France has enacted a digital-majority framework and the EU is rolling out wallet-compatible proof-of-age infrastructure.
assessments.counterSignal: Privacy-preserving selective disclosure, data-minimisation and non-centralised proof designs are documented safeguards; convergence does not prove covert motive.

assessments.rationale: IMF debt projections, ECB financial-stability analysis and tighter bank lending standards show elevated sovereign, funding and household-credit pressure.
assessments.counterSignal: Capital, liquidity, central-bank facilities and surveillance systems remain stronger than during earlier banking crises.

assessments.rationale: Climate, water, fertiliser, demographic and regulatory pressures are materially affecting farm income, adaptation and domestic production resilience.
assessments.counterSignal: Diversification, adaptation support, domestic-input policy and resilience investment are active and can lower dependence.
